Your first step is in this email. Do it before October 20.

The 7-week challenge

You're in the 7-week challenge. Once a week from October 20 to December 1, you'll get one email with one action and a time to do it. Seven weeks, seven small decisions.

Your first step, starting now

Print this worksheet: Step 1: What type of man do you want to be?

Give it twenty minutes, one sitting, with a pen. You'll finish with one sentence that says who you're becoming. Every week after this gets checked against that sentence.

Pick your brother

Send this link to one man you trust and ask him to do it with you: bethemansystem.com/7-week-challenge

Once a week, text each other one word: done, or missed. That's the whole accountability. Tracking works better when someone else sees it.

If you joined after October 20, don't go back and catch up. Do this step this week, and pick up with the next week's email.

Brian

week-1.subject: Week 1: one sentence
week-1.preview: Before any goal, decide who is doing it.
week-1.html:
Before any goal, decide who is doing it.

The 7-week challenge

Week one of the 7-week challenge starts today.

Most men start with goals. That's why the goals don't hold. A goal with no man behind it is a wish with a deadline. So this week you decide who is doing it.

This week's action

By Thursday at 9 PM, finish the Step 1 worksheet: What type of man do you want to be? Twenty minutes, a pen, one sitting.

You'll end with one sentence. Something like: "I am a man who is home when he's home, keeps his word to his wife, and prays with his children before they sleep." Yours will be different. Write it anyway, even if it feels too big.

How you'll know you did it

  • The sentence is written down, not just thought about
  • Someone in your house could see it in you without being told
  • You texted your brother this week: done, or missed

Next week, that sentence decides which of your goals stay.

Brian

week-2.subject: Week 2: three goals, not ten
week-2.preview: If it doesn't answer to your sentence, it's somebody else's goal.
week-2.html:
If it doesn't answer to your sentence, it's somebody else's goal.

The 7-week challenge

Week two. Get last week's sentence in front of you.

Every man I talk to has ten things he's going to fix. Ten goals means none of them get a time. So this week you cut.

This week's action

Tonight, write down every goal you're carrying. All of them: the gym, the money, the temper, the phone, the prayer life, the side business. Then hold each one up against your sentence and ask: does this make me more like that man?

Keep three. Cross out the rest. Not forever, just for these seven weeks.

If a goal doesn't answer to your sentence, it's somebody else's goal: your father's, your pastor's, the man on your phone.

How you'll know you did it

  • You have exactly three goals written under your sentence
  • Each one connects to a word in that sentence
  • You texted your brother: done, or missed

Next week we look at what has stopped you before. Bring honesty.

Brian

week-3.subject: Week 3: name the wall
week-3.preview: It was probably the same thing every time.
week-3.html:
It was probably the same thing every time.

The 7-week challenge

Week three.

You didn't fall short for lack of wanting it. Something stopped you, and it was probably the same thing every time. A plan that depended on how you felt. One bad day that turned into a bad month. An evening with no decision in it. A habit you inherited and never agreed to.

Mine was meaning it. I meant it every single time, and I changed nothing for years.

This week's action

Pick one of your three goals. Think back to the last time it fell apart. Write one sentence that finishes this: "It stopped when..."

Be plain about it. "It stopped when I got home tired and turned on the TV" is useful. "I lacked discipline" isn't. You can't build around a wall you won't look at.

How you'll know you did it

  • You wrote down a moment, not a character flaw
  • You'd recognise that moment if it happened again this week
  • You texted your brother: done, or missed

Next week, that moment gets a plan with a time on it.

Brian

week-4.subject: Week 4: give it a time
week-4.preview: "Weekly" is not a time. Thursday at 7:40 is.
week-4.html:
"Weekly" is not a time. Thursday at 7:40 is.

The 7-week challenge

Week four. This is the one that changes things.

Nothing exists until it has a time. "I'll be more present" is a goal. "Monday and Thursday, 7:40 PM, phone in the kitchen drawer until the kids are in bed" is a system.

Across many studies, people who wrote down when and where they'd act were measurably more likely to follow through than people who only decided to. In one, 91% of the planners did it, against 38% of everyone else.

This week's action

Take the goal from last week, the one with the wall in front of it. Write it as: day, time, place, action. Put it right where the wall was. If it stopped when you got home tired, the time is the moment you walk through the door.

Then do it at least once before next week's email.

How you'll know you did it

  • It has a day and a clock time, not "evenings" or "weekly"
  • You did it at least once this week
  • You texted your brother: done, or missed

Brian

P.S. This is Step 4 of the Be The Man framework. All seven steps, each with its worksheet, are in the Club, plus a monthly call with me and an accountability partner: bethemansystem.com/the-club

week-5.subject: Week 5: decide what a miss is
week-5.preview: So one bad day doesn't cost you a month.
week-5.html:
So one bad day doesn't cost you a month.

The 7-week challenge

Week five. By now you've probably missed at least once. Good. That's what this week is for.

Here's how most promises die: you miss one day, you feel like a failure, and by Friday you've quit the whole thing. The miss wasn't the problem. Not knowing what a miss means was.

This week's action

Under your day-and-time plan, write two lines:

  • A miss is: (for example, "the phone wasn't in the drawer by 7:45")
  • When I miss, I: (for example, "tell my wife that night and do it the next evening")

That's a failure condition. Decide it before the bad day comes, so the bad day doesn't get to decide for you.

How you'll know you did it

  • Your miss is something you could see, not a feeling
  • Your recovery happens within a day, not "next week"
  • You texted your brother: done, or missed

Next week is a holiday week. That's on purpose.

Brian

week-6.subject: Week 6: count it
week-6.preview: Four out of seven is four out of seven. Not "going well."
week-6.html:
Four out of seven is four out of seven. Not "going well."

The 7-week challenge

Week six, and it's Thanksgiving week. Travel, family, late nights, a full house. This is exactly the kind of week your system has to survive.

Numbers as numbers, not stories. Four out of seven is four out of seven. Not "going well." Not "pretty good considering."

This week's action

On a piece of paper, draw seven boxes, one for each day from today to next Monday. Every night, mark your one action: a check if you did it at the time you set, an X if you missed. Fill it in that night, not from memory on Sunday.

When next week's email arrives, write the number at the bottom: something out of seven.

How you'll know you did it

  • Every box is filled in, checks and X's both
  • You have a number, not a description
  • You texted your brother: done, or missed, every night this week

If you want a tracker that adds itself up, the Weekly Scorecard does it for a whole quarter ($7): bethemansystem.com/products. Paper works fine.

Happy Thanksgiving. Next week is the last one.

Brian

week-7.subject: Week 7: God at the center
week-7.preview: The last week, and the test that matters.
week-7.html:
The last week, and the test that matters.

The 7-week challenge

The last week.

A system with you at the center will serve you. That's the problem. Built around yourself, even a good system becomes a more efficient way to get what you want. So the center isn't you. The man in your sentence from week one starts as the man God is making.

This week's action

Take everything you've written over seven weeks: the sentence, the three goals, the wall, the time, the miss, the number. Lay it out together. Then pray over it, out loud if you can, and ask one question: is this who God is making me, or who I want to look like?

Change anything that answers the wrong way.

The real test

Could someone in your house tell something changed in these seven weeks, without you telling them? Don't ask them. Just watch this week.

Text your brother one last time. Then decide whether you're done, or whether this was the start.

If this was the start
